🎲 Welcome to Incarnos

Incarnos is a pen & paper roleplaying game, like D&D or Pathfinder, but built to be easy to learn.

How a session works

  • You play a hero you create yourself (see @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.LB12t6WX29ZuE2km]{Character Creation}).
  • The GM describes the situation. You say what your character does.
  • If the outcome is uncertain, you roll a die. The GM tells you what happens.

What you need: a PC with a browser (we play in Foundry), a headset, your character, and some friends.

Read next

  1. The core roll (below)
  2. @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.LB12t6WX29ZuE2km]{Character Creation}
  3. @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.GIkBBbVn23hPw44l]{Attributes And Stats}
  4. @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.eCuTVrCwXuSIkDQ7]{List Of Actions} (combat and conditions)
  5. @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.cOYAUSZXJLbuGekb]{Magic} (spells and Incarna)

Everything else you learn while playing. Questions? Just ask the GM or another player.

🎯 The core roll

Almost every roll works the same way: roll a d20 and get at or below the number you roll against.

Str 12, Str check → roll 12 or lower and you succeed.

  • Natural 1: always a success, and a critical one. On an attack: maximum damage.
  • Natural 20: always a failure, and a critical one. On an attack: roll on the critical failure table.
  • Advantage: roll 2d20, keep the lower. Disadvantage: roll 2d20, keep the higher.

Modifiers are added to the number you roll against. Minus is always bad for you, plus is always good.

Str 12 with −2 → roll 10 or lower.

Check, save, contest

  • Check: roll under a stat (Dex check).
  • Save: roll under a save value to resist something (Con save against poison).
  • Contest: two creatures against each other. Both roll d(20 − stat) (at least a d2). Lower total wins; on a tie, roll again.

🧙 Creating a character

You choose six things:

  1. Race
  2. Element (your magic)
  3. Stats
  4. One talent
  5. A weapon
  6. (optional) Up to 4 experiences

Incarnos is an open system: want something that doesn't exist yet, like a new race, element, spell or talent? Talk to the GM. The GM balances it and can say no if it doesn't fit the world.

Where to look things up: in Foundry, open the Compendium tab: Incarnos Races, Talents, Weapons and Spells are always up to date.

1–2 · Race and element

Race: pick one from the list. You can also build your own with the GM; it gets one of these bonuses:

  • 1 strong talent
  • 1 weaker talent + 1 stat point
  • 2 stat points

Your own race also needs a culture, look and history.

Element: pick one. Each element has its own spells and a speciality (Fire: area damage, Water: healing, Earth: protection, …) and an affinity (e.g. a resistance). You can also invent a new element with the GM.

3 · Stats

All 8 stats start at 5. You get 48 cost points to raise them. Higher values cost more:

  • 5 → 11: 1 point per step
  • 12 → 14: 2 points per step
  • 15 → 16: 3 points per step
  • 17 → 18: 4 points per step
  • 19 → 20: 5 points per step

Or take a ready-made array and spread it over your stats as you like:

  • Generalist: 11 / 11 / 11 / 11 / 11 / 11 / 11 / 11
  • Specialist: 14 / 14 / 11 / 11 / 9 / 9 / 7 / 7
  • Struggling Prodigy: 16 / 11 / 11 / 11 / 11 / 9 / 7 / 5

An average person has 10 in every stat, so your hero starts above average. What each stat does: @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.GIkBBbVn23hPw44l]{Attributes And Stats}.

4–6 · Talent, weapon, experiences

Talent: pick one. Talents are special abilities: born ones (flying, tough skin, resistance) or learned ones (brewing, athletics, performing).

Weapon: every character has one, and fists count too. Strength weapons (clubs, hammers, greatswords) attack with Str, Dexterity weapons (daggers, bows) with Dex. With neither high Str nor high Dex you will rarely hit, so plan for one of them.

Experiences (optional): up to 4 small background traits, like a former job or a habit from your past. They work like small talents: a slight bonus on fitting checks.

🍅 The 8 stats

Explained the tomato way:

  • Strength (Str): crushing a tomato. → melee attacks, Health
  • Dexterity (Dex): hitting a far-away target with a tomato. → ranged attacks, Parry
  • Constitution (Con): not throwing up after a bad tomato. → Health, physical saves
  • Willpower (Wil): eating a bad tomato anyway. → Incarna, mental saves
  • Perception (Prc): finding wild tomatoes in the forest. → Parry, initiative, noticing things
  • Speed (Spd): catching a falling tomato 5 m away. → movement, initiative
  • Intelligence (Int): knowing a tomato is a fruit. → spells, Incarna
  • Charisma (Cha): selling a tomato fruit salad. → spells, persuading people

Every stat is also used for fitting checks: lifting a rock (Str), holding your breath (Con), persuading someone (Cha).

📊 Values from your stats

Always round down.

  • Health (HP) = 2 × Con + Str. At 0 HP you fall unconscious.
  • Incarna (IP) = 2 × Wil + Int. The elemental energy you spend on spells.
  • Parry = (2 × Prc + Dex) ÷ 3. Roll under it to avoid an attack.
  • Saves protect you from spells and effects:
    • Str, Dex, Spd, Con save = (2 × stat + Con) ÷ 3
    • Wil, Prc, Int, Cha save = (2 × stat + Wil) ÷ 3
  • Movement = Spd ÷ 2 squares per move (1 square = 1.5 m). Spd 10 → 5 squares = 7.5 m
  • Initiative = Prc + Spd + 1d20 at the start of a fight. Highest goes first.
  • Action points (AP): 3 per turn.

Your race, talents and items can add to these (e.g. +1 Parry).

⚔️ Combat basics

Turn order: everyone rolls initiative. On your turn you have 3 AP. Moving, attacking, casting and most other actions cost AP.

Attacking: roll under Str (melee) or Dex (ranged), plus your weapon's hitrate, plus the target's Parry modifier. Hit = the d20 is at or below that.

Str 13, weapon hitrate +1, target Parry modifier −2 → roll 12 or lower.

Defending: when you are attacked, roll under your Parry plus the attack's modifier (the GM tells you, e.g. Melee −2). Success = you parry it.

Damage: your weapon's damage dice. Weapon traits can change them.

Critical hit: a natural 1 on an attack (weapon or spell) maxes the damage dice. 1d8 + 2 → 10 damage.

Good to know

  • Hitting another player character deals half damage.
  • Elites act 2 times per round, bosses 3 times.
  • Reactions (Opportunity Attack, Help, Guard Ally) also cost AP. All actions and reactions are in the action list.

🩹 Conditions

  • Prone: melee attacks against you are easier, ranged ones harder. You can only Crawl or Stand Up.
  • Grappled: you can't move.
  • Hidden: advantage on your attacks and Parries.
  • Hindered: your next attack has disadvantage.
  • Intimidated: disadvantage on checks against the intimidator, who has advantage against you.
  • Taunted: you must attack the taunter.
  • Asleep: you can't act. Each action you would take removes 1 sleep token instead. Taking damage halves your tokens, rounded up (min. 2).
  • Mounted: you ride on a bigger creature and have advantage on attacks against it.

Token conditions: at the start of your turn they trigger, then you lose 1 token.

  • Burn / Poisoned / Bleed: 1 damage per token. Burn ends with 1 AP or water. Any healing ends Bleed, but not Poison.
  • Regenerating: heal 1d6 + the caster's level.
  • Dying (0 HP): you fall prone and have 1 action per turn. The GM rolls a hidden death save each turn: 1-10 success, 11-20 failure, nat 1 heals 1 HP, nat 20 = two failures, damage = one failure. 3 successes: stable (usually Unconscious). 3 failures: dead. Healing ends it.
  • Barrier: the next damage you'd take is ignored completely, then the Barrier ends (Bubblebarrier also heals 1d4 each turn).
  • Blinded: disadvantage on attacks, Parry rolls and saves; 1 token less at the end of your turn.
  • Shadowmarked: marked by shadows (Shadowbomb only hits marked creatures).
  • Shadowform: +3 Parry, Shadowstrike deals 4d8 + (lvl * 2).
  • Shadowclone: 1 extra action; when an enemy attacks you, a d20 of 9 or lower hits the clone instead (the clone stays for the turn).
  • Frenzied: next turn you attack random creatures within reach, friend or foe, even while asleep.
  • Charged: each token gives 1 extra action at the start of a turn.
  • Paralyzed: you lose 1 action on your next turn (doesn't stack).
  • Stunned: you lose all your actions on your next turn (doesn't stack).
  • Unconscious: stable at 0 HP; you can't act or move until you're healed.
  • Summoned: a summon loses 1 token at the end of its summoner's turn and vanishes at 0.

✨ Magic and Incarna

Elements: every spell belongs to an element (Fire, Water, Plants, Shadow, …) or is elementless (Physical, Luck). Each element gives its users an affinity, e.g. a resistance.

Incarna (IP): the elemental energy in your body. Every spell costs IP and, in combat, AP. You have 2 × Wil + Int IP.

Casting a spell

  • Attack spells: roll under the spell's stat (e.g. Int / Cha: use the higher one) plus the target's Parry modifier. A natural 1 maxes the damage dice.
  • Spells with (3x) attack 3 times. Every hit deals its own damage.
  • Save spells: the target rolls a save. A bonus on the spell makes that save harder for the enemy.
  • Targets: Enemy = not on your side. Ally = on your side, never yourself. Target = anyone, yourself included. Friendlies = your side, yourself included. Up to 5 Enemies: pick 1-5 enemies in range.
  • Area spells hit everyone in the area, except invisible creatures. An area spell for Enemies or Friendlies only hits that side.

Weave (1 AP, no IP): a small burst of raw magic. Roll under Int or Cha; deals 1d8 damage.

Weakness and resistance: damage of an element a creature is weak to is doubled; damage it resists is halved. Elementless damage is never doubled or halved.

All spells are in Foundry under Compendium → Incarnos Spells.

⬆️ Levelling up

You earn experience (XP) in sessions; important sessions give more. When you reach the total, you level up.

Level · XP total · known spells

  • 1 · 0 XP · 1 spell
  • 2 · 10 XP · 2 spells
  • 3 · 30 XP · 3 spells
  • 4 · 80 XP · 4 spells
  • 5 · 160 XP · 7 spells + 1 level-2 spell
  • 6 · 300 XP · 8 spells + 1 level-2 spell

Raising stats costs the same as at character creation:

  • 5 → 11: 1 point per step
  • 12 → 14: 2 points
  • 15 → 16: 3 points
  • 17 → 18: 4 points
  • 19 → 20: 5 points

GM only

Foundry follows this note; the drafts in zbuild a system are outdated where they disagree. Every section is written so it can also be posted on Discord as it is.

1. The core roll

  • Almost every roll is a d20 roll-under: roll a d20, and you succeed if the result is at or below the value you roll against (a stat, a save, your Parry).
  • Natural 1: always a success, and a critical one (extra effects). On an attack it is a critical hit: see Combat.
  • Natural 20: always a failure, and a critical one (extra effects). On an attack roll, roll on @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.UGjhptqxo3qJ1oSq]{Critical Failures} (d10 for how bad, then that table).
  • Advantage: roll 2d20 and keep the lower. Disadvantage: roll 2d20 and keep the higher.

2. Modifiers (absolute rule)

  • A negative modifier is always bad for players, a positive modifier always good. This holds everywhere: attacks, Parry, saves, checks, monster stat blocks, spells.
  • Add the modifier to the value you roll under: −2 on Str 12 means you roll under 10.
  • Monster stat blocks are written for the players too: Melee -2 means you parry that attack at −2, ST Wil -3 means you make that Wil save at −3.
  • On your spells, the modifier on the enemy's save is also written for you: Target Save Wil+4 makes the enemy's save 4 harder.

3. Stats

Stat Used for
Strength (Str) melee attacks, Health
Dexterity (Dex) ranged attacks, Parry
Constitution (Con) Health, physical saves
Willpower (Wil) Incarna (IP), mental saves
Perception (Prc) Parry, initiative, noticing things
Speed (Spd) movement, initiative
Intelligence (Int) spells, Incarna (IP)
Charisma (Cha) social interaction, spells

4. Derived values

Round down every result.

  • Health (HP) = 2 × Con + Str
  • Incarna (IP) = 2 × Wil + Int — the elemental energy you spend on spells (formerly called MP or PP)
  • Parry = (2 × Prc + Dex) / 3
  • Saves:
    • Str, Dex, Spd and Con saves = (2 × stat + Con) / 3
    • Wil, Prc, Int and Cha saves = (2 × stat + Wil) / 3
  • Movement = Spd / 2 squares; 1 square = 1,5 m (Spd 10 → 5 squares = 7,5 m)
  • Initiative = Prc + Spd + 1d20, highest goes first
  • Action points (AP): 3 per turn

Race, talents and items can add to these (e.g. +1 Parry); those bonuses come on top.

5. Checks, saves and contests

  • Check: roll under the stat (Str check: d20 ≤ Str).
  • Save: roll under the save value of that stat (Con save: d20 ≤ Con save).
  • Contest (two creatures against each other): each side rolls d(20 − stat), at least a d2. The lower total wins; on a tie both roll again. Attack contests use the stat, save contests use the save value.

6. Combat

  • Each turn you have your AP (3). Moving, attacking, casting and most other actions cost AP; see the @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.uqPSylGIwGpke2QM]{action list}.
  • Attacking: roll under Str (melee) or Dex (ranged), plus your weapon's hitrate, plus the target's Parry modifier. The attack hits if the d20 is at or below that value.
  • Monsters' Parry: monsters don't roll Parry. Their Parry gives the modifier players get against them: 10 − Parry (Parry 10 → ±0, Parry 14 → −4, Parry 6 → +4). Stat blocks show both: Parry: 14 (-4).
  • Players' Parry: when you are attacked, roll under your Parry plus the attack modifier the GM announces (Melee -2 → roll under Parry − 2). If you succeed, you parry the attack.
  • Damage: the weapon's damage dice. @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.LdDQ8p7ZMeoHISyH]{Weapon traits} can change this (e.g. @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.LdDQ8p7ZMeoHISyH]{Deadly}, @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.LdDQ8p7ZMeoHISyH]{Fatal}, @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.LdDQ8p7ZMeoHISyH]{Critical Strike}).
  • Critical hit: a natural 1 on an attack roll (weapon or spell) maxes the damage dice: 1d8+2 deals 10, 6d6 deals 36. Deadly and Fatal change the dice first, then they are maxed. Critical Strike weapons crit on a wider range (e.g. 1–3).
  • Two-handed use (@UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.LdDQ8p7ZMeoHISyH]{Two-Hand} trait): −2 hitrate, bigger damage die.
  • PvP: when a player's attack or spell hits another player character, the damage is halved.
  • Elites and bosses: an Elite takes 2 turns per round, a Boss 3 turns. Each turn has its own initiative roll and full AP.
  • Attack variants, reactions, movement and conditions: see the @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.uqPSylGIwGpke2QM]{action list}.

7. Magic

  • Spells belong to an element (Fire, Water, Shadow, …) or are elementless (Physical, Luck). Each element has an affinity. All elements and spells: @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.UVfAGM0l290KWDFR]{Spells}.
  • A spell costs its IP and, in combat, its actions (AP). Some costs are variable (X Actions, X * 8 IP).
  • Spell attack: roll under the spell's stat (e.g. Attack Int / Cha: the higher of the two) plus the target's Parry modifier plus the spell's modifier. A natural 1 is a critical hit and maxes the spell's damage dice against that target.
  • Target save: the target rolls under its save value plus the spell's modifier (written for the caster's side, see Modifiers).
  • Range: every target must be within the spell's Range, counted from your token's edge to the target's edge (Touch / Melee: next to you, diagonals included). A placed area's centre must be within range. In Foundry a ring around the caster shows the range: green in range, red out of range.
  • Targets: a spell's Target says whom it may hit and how many. Enemy = a creature not on your side (in Foundry: another token disposition). Ally = someone on your side, never yourself. Target = anyone, yourself included. Friendlies = everyone on your side, yourself included. Up to 5 Enemies: pick 1–5 enemies within the spell's range. Enemies / Friendlies on an area spell: every enemy / friendly creature in the area.
  • Area spells (circle, line, rectangle) hit every creature in the area, but never an invisible one. In Foundry: tokens hidden from the players are skipped.
  • Weave (attack action, see the @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.uqPSylGIwGpke2QM]{action list}): roll under Int or Cha, 1d8 damage, no IP.
  • Weakness and Resistance: damage of an element a creature is weak to is doubled; damage of an element it resists is halved (round down). Elementless damage (Physical, Luck) is never doubled or halved.

8. Conditions and damage over time

  • Conditions (Prone, Grappled, Immobilized, Hidden, Hindered, Intimidated, Taunted, Asleep, Mounted, Paralyzed, Stunned, Barrier, Blinded, Shadowmarked, Shadowform, Shadowclone, Charged, Frenzied, Dying, Unconscious, Summoned) are explained in @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.VQ2NeN8KNFTmGhQJ]{Conditions} and the @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.uqPSylGIwGpke2QM]{action list}.
  • Burn, Poisoned and Bleed use tokens: Burn D4 gives 1d4 Burn tokens. At the start of your turn you take 1 damage per token, then remove 1 token.
    • Burn: spending 1 AP to put out the flames, or being doused with water, removes all Burn tokens.
    • Poisoned: healing does not remove Poison tokens.
    • Bleed: any healing removes all Bleed tokens. Bleeding to 0 HP kills.
  • Regenerating also uses tokens: Regenerating 2 lasts 2 turns. At the start of your turn you heal 1d6 + lvl (the level of whoever gave it, e.g. the caster of @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.spells.Item.1VicZhPOZvJWGzDT]{Leaf wind}; set by hand: your own level), then remove 1 token.
  • Damage from Burn, Poisoned and Bleed is dealt automatically at the start of your turn. Healing from Regenerating is offered to you in the chat (only you and the GM see it); apply it yourself.
  • Immobilized: you can't use movement actions; 1 AP breaks free (some sources ask for a roll). Immobilized 2 also ends on its own: remove 1 token at the end of each of your turns.
  • New tokens of the same kind are added to the ones you have.
  • 0 HP: Dying. A character who drops to 0 HP is Dying at once and falls Prone. While Dying you have only 1 action per turn. (Bleeding to 0 HP still kills outright, see Bleed.)
    • Death saves: at the start of each of your turns the GM rolls a hidden d20 for you. 1–10 is a success, 11–20 a failure. A natural 1 heals you 1 HP, a natural 20 counts as two failures. Taking damage while Dying counts as one failure. The GM shows the result when it fits the story.
    • 3 successes: you are stabilized and no longer Dying; you stay at 0 HP, usually Unconscious (you can't act or move until you regain HP). 3 failures: you die.
    • Any healing ends Dying (and Unconscious) and resets your death saves.
  • Summoned: a summoned creature has one Summoned token per turn it lasts; it loses one at the end of its summoner's turn and vanishes when the last is gone. The summoner can dismiss it at any time.

Traits are the special rules a weapon carries: how you hold it (Two-Hand, Agile), how it hits (Finesse, Critical Strike, Deadly) or what else it can do (Trip, Disarm, Pull). Some traits come with a limit written on the weapon, e.g. (Once per Shortrest).

Monster attacks use the same traits, so a trait works the same for heroes and monsters.

Weapon Traits

  • Agile: This weapon may be dual wielded.
  • Barbed (dice, e.g. 1d4): Deal the named dice amount of damage at the beginning of the target's turn for 3 turns.
  • @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.LdDQ8p7ZMeoHISyH]{Bloodsucker}
  • Consuming: Consumes the following item each use: (consumed item, e.g. arrows)
  • Critical Strike (range, e.g.1-2): Crits now occur on the listed range.
  • Deadly (dice, e.g. D4): When you crit, add the named dice to your damage roll (not doubled).
  • Disarm: You can use this weapon to Disarm with the Strength roll instead of attacking.
  • Fatal (dice, e.g. D4): When you crit, the weapon’s damage die increases to the named die size instead of the normal die size.
  • Finesse: You can use your Dexterity instead of your Strength on attacks rolls using this melee weapon.
  • (Cooldown 1 turn) Flama Diddle: Your weapon may now attack with incendiary projectiles that deal 1d8 fire damage for 1 action. When greased enemies are hit, the target take additional 2d8 fire damage.
  • Forceful: When you attack with it more than once on your turn, the second attack gains +2 damage, and each subsequent attack gains +4 damage
  • Grease Cannon: You are able to hit 4 squares in a line but must reload the weapon to use it again. Reloading costs 1 action.
  • (Once per Shortrest) Knockdown Sweep: Your next attack hits up to 3 targets in front of you and prones them instead of dealing damage.
  • (Once per Longrest) Multishot: Your normal attack deals half the damage but hits every enemy in a cone.
  • Nonlethal: This weapon cannot kill a target - only knock them out.
  • Parry: +1 Parry
  • (Once per Shortrest) Pommel Strike: A target must succeed a Con saving throw or be dazed.
  • Poor Precision: This weapon hits if you fail your attack roll and misses if you succeed your attack roll.
  • Power Shot (dice, e.g. D4): You may spend an additional action to add an additional named dice to your damage roll (doubled on crit).
  • Pull: You are able to pull your target up to your destination when you hit. The target may prevent that by succeeding a con saving throw.
  • Reach (range, e.g. 4,5m): This weapon can attack in melee within the named ranged.
  • Retaliation Knockback: When you parry an attack wearing this weapon, knock the attacker 3m back in an any direction.
  • (Once per Turn) Shield Bash: A medium or smaller target must succeed a Str saving throw or be knocked prone for one turn. This is not considered a weapon attack and therefore does not penalize the next weapon attack.
  • (Once per Longrest) Shotgun mode: For 1 round, you may turn your weapon into a shotgun. While in shotgun mode, your range becomes 3m and every action you do with your weapon cost 1 less action and can be used a maximum of 3times. After this, your weapon breaks and can only be reinstated by a Longrest.
  • Sling: You are able to sling semi-/ fluid substances with this weapon. In this scenario, the attack is considered a ranged weapon.
  • Spikey (dice, e.g. 1d4): Deal the named dice amount of damage to your character
  • Stealthy: This weapon does not reveal you when you attack from stealth.
  • Sweep: When you use Attack: Cleave, it deals full damage instead of 0.5× damage.
  • Throwable (range, e.g. 3m): You can throw this weapon as a ranged attack without penalty, and it is a ranged weapon when thrown.
  • @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.LdDQ8p7ZMeoHISyH]{Transfusion}
  • Trip: You can use this weapon to prone with the Strength roll instead of attacking.
  • Two-Hand (dice, e.g. D4): This weapon can be wielded with two hands - in this case your attack has -2 hitrate and deals the named dice dmg instead.
  • Unmanoeuvrable: If you use a movementaction this turn, you cannot attack anymore. Vice versa, if you attack this turn, you cannot use a movementaction anymore.

All magic belongs to an element. You pick one element and use its spells

  • Affinity: every element gives its users a passive bonus (Fire: resistance to fire damage). It is listed first under each element.
  • Reading a spell: Cost is the actions (AP, in combat) and the Incarna (IP) it takes. Range, Target, Check and Duration say how it is cast. Effect says what happens; the text below it is flavour.
  • Targets: Single Enemy = one enemy. Single Ally = one ally, never yourself. Single Target = anyone, yourself included. Conditions change what a creature can do: lying Prone, being Grappled or Hidden, being Taunted into attacking someone. Some work with tokens that count down each turn: damage over time (Burn, Poisoned, Bleed) and healing over time (Regenerating). Burn D4 means you get 1d4 Burn tokens. At 0 HP a character is Dying and makes death saves; a summoned creature counts its remaining turns as Summoned tokens.

In Foundry, conditions are the status icons on a token. Attacks, spells and @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.uqPSylGIwGpke2QM]{actions} that cause one put it on the target for you.

Conditions

  • Asleep: You cannot act. For every action you would act, you remove 1 sleep token. When you take damage while asleep, you half your sleep tokens, rounded up (min. 2 tokens).
  • Barrier: The next damage you would take is ignored completely, then Barrier ends. Otherwise you lose 1 Barrier token at the start of each of your turns, and Barrier ends when the last one is gone. Some barriers also heal you at the start of your turn while they last (Bubblebarrier: 1d4 HP). A new Barrier does not stack: it sets the turns to the longer of the two.
  • Bleed: You get that many Bleed tokens. At the start of your turn you take 1 damage per Bleed token, then remove 1 token. Any healing removes all Bleed tokens. If Bleed brings you to 0 HP, you bleed out and die.
  • Blinded: You have disadvantage on attacks, Parry rolls and saving throws. You lose 1 Blinded token at the end of each of your turns.
  • Burn: You get that many Burn tokens. At the start of your turn you take 1 damage per Burn token, then remove 1 token. Spending 1 AP to put out the flames, or being doused with water, removes all Burn tokens.
  • Charged: At the start of your turn, if you have a Charged token, you get 1 additional action this turn and lose 1 Charged token.
  • Dying: You are at 0 HP. You fall Prone and have only 1 action per turn. At the start of each of your turns the GM makes a hidden death save for you (d20): 1–10 is a success, 11–20 a failure. A natural 1 heals you 1 HP, a natural 20 counts as two failures. Taking damage while Dying counts as one failure. 3 successes: you are stabilized and no longer Dying (you stay at 0 HP, usually Unconscious). 3 failures: you die. Any healing ends Dying and resets your death saves.
  • Frenzied: On your next turn you must spend your actions attacking creatures within your reach, friend or foe: each attack goes to a randomly chosen creature within reach. If nobody is in reach, you move toward the nearest creature. You lash out even while Asleep (Asleep's rule for actions you spend still applies). Frenzied ends at the end of that turn.
  • Grappled: You cannot use movement actions.
  • Hidden: Your attacks have advantage while you remain hidden, your Parries are also advantaged.
  • Hindered: Your next attack has disadvantage.
  • Immobilized: You cannot use movement actions (Dash, Crawl, Disengage, ...). Spend 1 AP to break free; some sources ask for a roll first (e.g. Crystal Trap). With tokens (Immobilized 2) it also ends on its own: remove 1 token at the end of each of your turns.
  • Intimidated: You have disadvantage on checks against the intimidator. The intimidator has advantage on checks against you.
  • Mounted: You are mounted on a creature. You move with it and have advantage on attack rolls against it. You can only be mounted on a creature that is at least 1 size larger than you.
  • Paralyzed: You lose 1 action on your next turn. Paralyzed does not stack and ends at the start of that turn.
  • Poisoned: You get that many Poison tokens. At the start of your turn you take 1 damage per Poison token, then remove 1 token. Healing does not remove Poison tokens.
  • Prone: Your melee Parry rolls are disadvantaged, but your ranged Parry rolls are advantaged. Movement actions are limited to Crawl or Stand Up.
  • Regenerating: You have that many Regenerating tokens. At the start of your turn you heal 1d6 + lvl (the level of whoever gave it to you, e.g. the caster of Leaf wind; set by hand: your own level), then remove 1 token. The healing is offered to you in the chat; apply it yourself.
  • Shadowclone: A shadow clone stands with you. You get 1 additional action. When an enemy attacks you, roll a d20: on 9 or lower the clone is attacked instead and the attack does nothing to you. The clone stays until Shadowclone ends, however often it is attacked. You lose 1 Shadowclone token at the end of each of your turns.
  • Shadowform: You blend with the shadows: +3 Parry, and Shadowstrike deals 4d8 + (lvl * 2) shadow dmg instead of 2d8 + (lvl * 2). You lose 1 Shadowform token at the end of each of your turns.
  • Shadowmarked: You carry the mark of shadows. Some shadow spells (Shadowbomb) can only hit marked creatures. You lose 1 Shadowmarked token at the end of each of your turns.
  • Stunned: You lose all your actions on your next turn. Stunned does not stack and ends at the start of that turn.
  • Summoned: You are a summoned creature with that many Summoned tokens. At the end of your summoner's turn you lose 1 token; when the last one is gone, you vanish. Your summoner can dismiss you at any time.
  • Taunted: Your attacks must be targeted against the taunter. Taunted from a spell ends at the end of your next turn.
  • Unconscious: You are knocked out but stable at 0 HP. You cannot act or move, and you stay Prone. Ends when you regain HP.

Each turn you have 3 AP (action points). The action lists show everything you can spend them on: attacks, movement, reactions outside your turn, contests (Shove, Grapple, Taunt, …) and other actions like Dodge or Hide. Every action has its cost and a short Play Cheat to use at the table.

Core Attack Rules

  • Critical Hit: Rolling a natural 1 on a d20 is always a success and triggers additional effects. On an attack (weapon or spell), a critical hit maxes the damage dice: 1d8+2 deals 10. Traits that change crit damage (@UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.LdDQ8p7ZMeoHISyH]{Deadly}, @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.LdDQ8p7ZMeoHISyH]{Fatal}) apply first, then the dice are maxed. Weapons with @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.LdDQ8p7ZMeoHISyH]{Critical Strike} crit on a wider range.
  • Critical Failure: Rolling a natural 20 on a d20 is always a failure and triggers additional effects. On an attack roll, roll on @UUID[Compendium.incarnos.handbook.JournalEntry.DH2qKKNscN4oDRzo.JournalEntryPage.UGjhptqxo3qJ1oSq]{Critical Failures} (d10 for how bad, then that table).
  • Modifiers: a negative modifier is always bad for players, a positive one always good. Add it to the value you roll under: −2 on Str 12 means you roll under 10.
  • Attack Roll: The GM announces the target’s Parry modifier before the roll. Add it to the attribute you roll under, then roll. If the d20 is at or below the modified value, the attack hits.
  • Parry (monsters and GM-controlled NPCs): Monsters don’t roll Parry. Their Parry sets the modifier players apply to attacks against them: modifier = 10 − Parry (Parry 10 → ±0, 14 → −4, 6 → +4). Stat blocks list both, e.g. Parry: 14 (-4).
